hooks.command: echo "{\"hookSpecificOutput\":{\"hookEventName\":\"UserPromptSubmit\",\"additionalContext\":\"STANDING RULES (backoffice-final) - apply before responding: (1) Read this repo's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md first. (2) Fetch latest before investigating. Run git fetch origin and compare with origin/main for this repo and every sibling repo you read, before citing file contents or repo or deployment state as fact. A local checkout can be hundreds of commits behind. When you cannot or should not pull, read files with git show origin/main:<path>, and say so explicitly if you did not check. (3) Trace in the code, never from memory. Search the repo and its docs, trace the feature end to end, and cite file:line. (4) Label every claim verified, assumption or unknown. Never guess. (5) Explain the plan and wait for approval before any code change. Then make the smallest change that does the job. (6) Production is read-only. Do not run queries, deploy, change schema or invalidate caches unless explicitly instructed. (7) Update docs and README in the same change whenever the change affects what they describe. (8) Every SQL script must be idempotent. Re-running it is a no-op with the same end state. (9) Do not modify a sibling repo as a side effect of work here. Siblings are read-only references unless the user asks for a change in that repo. (10) Never print, log or commit a secret. Mask it if it must appear in a log line. (11) A new project or service ships with tests in the repo's existing test framework. (12) Commit, push or open a PR only when explicitly asked. \\\"Implement it\\\" authorizes local edits only. (13) Report validation with every change: build, unit tests, integration tests, manual checks and remaining risks. If something could not be validated, say what and why, name the tests to run before deployment, and mark the work Implementation Complete – Validation Pending, never Completed. (14) If a workflow step does not apply, say so instead of skipping it silently.\"}}"
